subtype: Approach: reciprocity by offering something useful [Thinking]
passage:
Subject: Thinking about what I can offer

Hi Uma,

I was about to write to Dr Rao again with another "please guide me". Then I stopped, because what do I give him? He is busy, and what I want is all take. So here is my plan. He has an open-source tool for cleaning survey data, and there is a bug list. I will actually try it on my own project, note any confusing steps, and send him two clear pages. I also went to the workshop last week; I can send my notes from the sessions he missed. Hopefully it helps and starts a proper conversation. What do you think? Is that presumptuous?

Rukmini

qa.q: What will Rukmini try on the project?
qa.a: Rukmini will try the open-source tool for cleaning survey data on the project.

qa.q: What is Rukmini feeling as the email is written?
qa.a: Rukmini feels hopeful but a bit unsure, ending with a question about whether the plan is presumptuous.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Rukmini use if the offer is ignored, and why?
qa.a: Rukmini could join the tool's public discussion and answer a beginner's question, because helping in public shows the same goodwill without needing a private reply.

qa.q: How might Dr Rao see this offer?
qa.a: Dr Rao would receive two clear pages about his own tool from a real user, which gives something useful instead of another request for guidance.

grounding: Shows building a relationship on what one can give, such as testing a tool or sharing notes, instead of only asking.
